WART (VERRUCA) Etiology Human papillomaviruses (HPVs) cause a spectrum of diseases from warts (verrucae vulgaris) to squamous cell carcinoma of the skin and mucous membranes, including the larynx. The HPVs are classified by genus, species, and type. More than 200 types are known, and the entire genomes of approximately 100 are completely sequenced. The incidence of all types of warts is highest in children and adolescents. HPV is spread by direct contact and autoinoculation; transmission within families and by fomites also occurs. The clinical manifestations of infection develop 1 month or longer after inoculation and depend on the HPV type, the size of the inoculum, the immune status of the host, and the anatomic site.
